item.content:encoded:
The Asia Climate Solutions (ACS) Design Grant 2026 is now accepting applications from organizations and consortiums developing innovative blended finance solutions that can mobilize private capital for climate action across Southeast Asia. Delivered through Convergence Blended Finance, the programme combines catalytic grant funding with acceleration support to help promising climate finance solutions progress from early-stage design and feasibility work toward implementation, investment readiness, and scale.

Supported by the Australian Government through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), the current funding cycle focuses specifically on solutions addressing climate-resilient agriculture, food security, and nature-based solutions in eligible Southeast Asian markets.

Selected organizations can access catalytic grants of up to AUD 350,000, depending on the maturity and type of project proposed. In addition to financial support, successful applicants can receive technical guidance, connections to investors and ecosystem partners, access to blended finance knowledge and data, training opportunities, and peer learning through the Convergence network.

The deadline to submit concept notes is September 28, 2026 at 9:00 PM ET, corresponding to September 29, 2026 at 9:00 AM SGT.

About the Asia Climate Solutions Design Grant

The Asia Climate Solutions Design Grant is part of Convergence’s regional blended finance accelerator initiatives. Its overarching objective is to catalyze innovative financial solutions capable of mobilizing substantial private investment into climate mitigation and adaptation activities in developing Asian markets.

Blended finance can play an important role in addressing investment barriers by strategically combining public, philanthropic, and private capital. Through the ACS Design Grant, Convergence aims to support commercially viable models that can use this approach to unlock investment while delivering measurable climate and development outcomes.

For the current funding cycle, particular attention is being placed on climate-resilient agriculture and nature-based solutions across Southeast Asia.

Agriculture remains critical to Southeast Asia’s economies, livelihoods, employment, and food security. It accounts for approximately 10% of regional GDP and employs roughly one-third of the workforce. At the same time, Southeast Asia holds around 30% of the world’s potential for nature-based solutions.

However, climate change, environmental degradation, and persistent financing gaps continue to limit investment in resilient agricultural systems and natural ecosystems. Women farmers can face additional challenges, including barriers to finance, productive resources, and markets.

The ACS Design Grant seeks to address these challenges by supporting innovative blended finance models capable of attracting capital into solutions that strengthen resilience while creating environmental, social, and economic benefits.

Who Supports the Asia Climate Solutions Programme?

Asia Climate Solutions is a multi-donor funded programme.

Its supporters include:

  • Australian Government through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
  • Olayan Group
  • UBS Optimus Foundation
  • The Rockefeller Foundation
  • Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS)

DFAT is supporting the current funding cycle focused on climate-resilient agriculture and nature-based solutions in Southeast Asia.

What Does the ACS Design Grant Offer?

The Accelerator provides two major forms of assistance to selected organizations:

  1. Catalytic Grant Funding
  2. Acceleration Support

Together, these components are intended to help organizations develop stronger blended finance structures, overcome early-stage barriers, engage potential investors, and move promising financial vehicles toward launch and scale.

1. Catalytic Grant Funding of Up to AUD 350,000

Eligible organizations can seek catalytic funding to support the development of blended finance solutions from feasibility and early-stage scoping through proof-of-concept activities.

Depending on the stage of development, funding may support activities such as:

  • Financial structuring
  • Legal structuring
  • Market scoping
  • Investment pipeline development
  • Stakeholder consultations
  • Investor outreach
  • Fundraising
  • Piloting
  • Governance framework development
  • Impact measurement framework development
  • Refinement of investment models
  • Preparation for potential vehicle launch

Funding levels depend on whether an applicant is seeking support for a Feasibility Study or a Proof-of-Concept.

2. Acceleration Support

Successful applicants will receive more than grant funding. Convergence also provides acceleration assistance intended to strengthen the investment model and help teams progress toward mobilizing capital.

Acceleration support may include:

  • Ongoing technical feedback and guidance to refine investment models and strategies
  • Opportunities to connect with Convergence’s network of investors and ecosystem partners
  • Support in expanding partnerships and identifying opportunities to mobilize resources for climate action
  • Access to Convergence member training
  • Access to blended finance data
  • Market insights and intelligence
  • Peer-learning opportunities

This combination of capital and technical assistance can be particularly valuable for organizations attempting to take an innovative climate finance concept and develop it into an investable and scalable structure.

Types of Asia Climate Solutions Design Grants

Applicants can apply under one of two principal grant categories based on the maturity of their proposed blended finance solution.

Feasibility Study Grant

The Feasibility Study Grant is designed for solutions at an earlier stage of development where organizations need to explore and validate whether a proposed blended finance vehicle is feasible.

Applicants should already have an initial design and structure for their proposed blended finance vehicle, an impact and investment thesis, and evidence of early stakeholder engagement.

What Can Feasibility Study Funding Be Used For?

Activities can include:

  1. Scoping and refining the design of the proposed vehicle
  2. Developing or refining the financial structure
  3. Developing or refining the legal structure
  4. Conducting market scoping
  5. Building an initial investment pipeline
  6. Conducting stakeholder consultations
  7. Developing draft impact assessment frameworks
  8. Developing governance frameworks

Feasibility Study Funding Amount

Organizations applying for a Feasibility Study Grant can seek up to AUD 200,000.

The funding is provided as a non-repayable grant.

Proof-of-Concept Grant

The Proof-of-Concept Grant targets solutions that have progressed further in their development.

At this stage, funding can support the design and structuring work necessary to prepare a blended finance vehicle for its possible launch.

Applicants should generally have already refined areas including their:

  • Financial model
  • Capital structure
  • Impact analysis
  • Governance approach

They should also demonstrate advanced engagement with potential investors.

What Can Proof-of-Concept Funding Support?

Examples include:

  1. Advancing fundraising activities
  2. Conducting investor outreach
  3. Refining the blended finance vehicle’s design
  4. Refining the vehicle’s legal structure
  5. Strengthening governance arrangements
  6. Refining impact frameworks
  7. Developing the investment pipeline
  8. Undertaking other structuring work needed to prepare the vehicle for potential launch

Proof-of-Concept Funding Amount

Proof-of-Concept applicants can seek up to AUD 350,000.

Funding may be provided as either a non-repayable or conditionally repayable grant.

What Types of Blended Finance Solutions Are Eligible?

Proposals must demonstrate a clear need for catalytic grant support for the design and/or launch of an innovative blended finance vehicle.

The proposed solution must be a financial instrument incorporating a blended finance structure.

Examples of potentially eligible structures include:

  • Funds
  • Project finance vehicles
  • Private companies
  • Bonds
  • Results-based financing structures
  • Financing facilities
  • Other suitable financial instruments incorporating blended finance

Importantly, proposed vehicles must demonstrate the potential to mobilize private investment at scale while generating development impact in Southeast Asia.

Solutions must also target climate mitigation and/or climate adaptation within the eligible sectors for this funding cycle.

Eligible Countries for the ACS Design Grant 2026

Proposed solutions must target one or more of the following Southeast Asian countries:

  • Cambodia
  • Indonesia
  • Lao PDR
  • Malaysia
  • Myanmar
  • Philippines
  • Thailand
  • Timor-Leste
  • Vietnam

A solution may operate within a single eligible country or across several eligible countries.

An important feature of the programme is that the applicant organization itself does not have to be domiciled in one of these countries.

However, the end beneficiaries and activities targeted by the proposed solution must be located within the eligible markets.

This means organizations based outside Southeast Asia may potentially participate provided their proposed blended finance solution satisfies the programme’s geographic and other eligibility requirements.

Priority Sector 1: Climate-Resilient Agriculture and Food Security

One of the major priorities for this funding round is developing financial models capable of improving resilience throughout agriculture and food systems.

Eligible areas include:

Climate-Smart and Regenerative Agriculture

Solutions may address climate-smart agricultural practices, regenerative agriculture, sustainable aquaculture, and related approaches that increase resilience while reducing environmental impacts.

Agricultural Value Chains

The programme can support blended finance solutions targeting agricultural value chains, including processing and improved market access.

Farmer, Cooperative and Agri-SME Finance

Solutions can focus on improving access to finance for farmers, agricultural cooperatives, and small and medium-sized enterprises operating within agricultural systems.

Agricultural Insurance and Climate Risk Management

Innovative financing structures that improve agricultural insurance or help communities and businesses manage climate-related risks may also qualify.

Agri-Tech and Smart Farming

The programme also identifies agricultural technology, biotechnology, and smart farming as eligible areas.

Priority Sector 2: Nature-Based Solutions

The ACS Design Grant also seeks innovative financing approaches that can unlock capital for nature-based solutions.

Eligible areas include:

  • Sustainable forestry
  • Landscape restoration
  • Ecosystem management
  • Carbon markets
  • Natural capital finance
  • Biodiversity finance
  • Blue carbon
  • Biodiversity conservation
  • Ecosystem restoration
  • Coastal protection
  • Watershed management
  • Ecosystem resilience

Applicants proposing solutions within these areas should demonstrate how blended finance can overcome investment barriers and help mobilize public, philanthropic, and private capital.

Eligibility Requirements for Applicant Organizations

Applications are only accepted from organizations or consortiums of organizations.

Potentially eligible organizations include:

  • Asset owners
  • Asset managers
  • Advisory firms
  • Foundations
  • Not-for-profit organizations
  • Private enterprises
  • Consortiums comprising eligible organizations

The lead organization must be capable of providing:

  1. Proof of incorporation
  2. Financial statements for the previous fiscal year

Individual applicants are therefore not the target applicants for this funding opportunity.

Beyond organizational eligibility, applicants must demonstrate that their proposed solution meets the programme’s purpose, geographic, sectoral, and blended finance requirements.

How Applications Will Be Evaluated

Convergence evaluates eligible proposals against seven major areas. Organizations preparing concept notes should carefully consider each of these criteria because they provide a strong indication of what assessors will be looking for.

1. Development Impact and Gender Considerations

Proposed blended finance solutions should deliver inclusive, measurable, and significant environmental and social impact.

Gender considerations should be intentionally integrated into areas such as:

  • Design
  • Governance
  • Implementation
  • Stakeholder engagement

Applicants should establish clear key performance indicators and include gender-related indicators where appropriate.

Recognized global standards should also be used to measure, monitor, and report impact.

2. Track Record and Capabilities

Evaluators will consider the applicant organization’s ability to successfully develop and manage the proposed solution.

Considerations include:

  • Relevant experience designing investment vehicles
  • Experience managing investment vehicles
  • Commitment of the core project team
  • Local presence within target markets
  • Partnerships within eligible countries

Applicants should therefore clearly demonstrate that their team has the experience, resources, partnerships, and commitment required to move the proposal forward.

3. Additionality

Applicants need to explain why blended finance is necessary.

The proposal should demonstrate:

  • A clear market gap
  • A strong rationale for using blended finance
  • Potential to unlock capital in the targeted markets
  • Potential to create new investable opportunities
  • Strategic use of ACS catalytic funding
  • Strategic use of ACS acceleration support

The grant is intended to address genuine barriers rather than simply replace capital that could readily be obtained elsewhere.

4. Scalability and Replicability

Convergence is seeking solutions with the potential to grow beyond a small pilot or isolated intervention.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • A clear capital structure
  • A credible fundraising strategy
  • Potential to mobilize significant private capital
  • A realistic pathway to reach the proposed target size
  • Potential to scale the solution
  • Opportunities to replicate the model across additional markets

Solutions with a credible pathway to expansion and replication can potentially generate a broader demonstration effect across the climate finance ecosystem.

5. Innovation and Demonstration Effect

The proposed solution should have the potential to generate useful lessons for the broader blended finance field.

Innovation could involve creating an entirely new financing model or applying an existing model within a new market or context.

Evaluators will consider whether other practitioners could learn from, adapt, or replicate the approach.

6. Likelihood of Achieving Financial Close

Applicants should demonstrate that the proposed structure has a credible pathway toward financial close.

This includes consideration of:

  • Bankability
  • Alignment with potential investors’ risk-return expectations
  • Progress already made toward financial close
  • Clear next steps
  • Appropriate risk management
  • Robust governance arrangements

A strong proposal should demonstrate not only an innovative idea but also a realistic pathway toward becoming an operational and investable vehicle.

7. Stakeholder Support

Applicants should demonstrate support from relevant internal and external stakeholders within the target country or region.

Proposals should show:

  • Engagement with important local partners
  • Support from key stakeholders
  • Clearly defined roles
  • A credible stakeholder engagement strategy
  • Appropriate partnerships to support the proposed launch

Local relationships can be particularly important in demonstrating market understanding and implementation capability.

Importance of Gender Considerations

Gender inclusion is specifically incorporated into the programme’s evaluation framework.

Applicants should consider how women and other relevant groups may experience different barriers within agricultural, financial, environmental, and climate systems.

For example, women farmers may encounter constraints in accessing finance, productive resources, and markets. Proposed financing solutions should therefore consider whether their design can address these barriers and produce inclusive outcomes.

Where appropriate, proposals should include measurable gender-related indicators and explain how gender considerations will influence the solution’s governance, implementation, and stakeholder engagement.

Asia Climate Solutions Design Grant Information Session

Convergence and Australia’s DFAT will host a virtual information session on September 10, 2026 for prospective applicants.

The session will provide an opportunity to learn more about:

  • Convergence’s Blended Finance Accelerator
  • The Asia Climate Solutions Design Grant
  • Current funding priorities
  • Grant eligibility requirements
  • Evaluation criteria
  • The application process

Participants will also have an opportunity to ask questions.

The session is scheduled for September 10, 2026 at 10:00 AM Singapore Time (SGT/GMT+8).

Prospective applicants are encouraged to participate, particularly organizations that need additional clarification about the programme’s requirements before preparing their concept notes.

For detailed evaluation criteria and scoring, refer to the Evaluation Criteria document

Application Deadline

The deadline to submit concept notes for the Asia Climate Solutions Design Grant is September 28, 2026 at 9:00 PM Eastern Time (ET), equivalent to September 29, 2026 at 9:00 AM Singapore Time (SGT).

Organizations interested in applying should avoid waiting until the final day, particularly where consortium partners, supporting documentation, financial information, and internal approvals need to be coordinated.

How to Apply for the Asia Climate Solutions Design Grant 2026

Interested organizations should review the full eligibility and evaluation requirements before beginning an application.

Applicants should particularly ensure that:

  1. The applicant is an eligible organization or consortium.
  2. The lead organization can provide proof of incorporation.
  3. The lead organization can provide financial statements for the previous fiscal year.
  4. The proposed solution incorporates a genuine blended finance structure.
  5. There is a clear rationale for catalytic grant funding.
  6. The solution targets climate mitigation and/or adaptation.
  7. Target activities and beneficiaries are located in one or more eligible Southeast Asian countries.
  8. The solution falls within climate-resilient agriculture, food security, or eligible nature-based solution sectors.
  9. The proposed vehicle demonstrates potential to mobilize private capital.
  10. The team can demonstrate relevant capabilities, partnerships, and a credible pathway toward implementation and scale.

Applicants should then prepare and submit their concept note through the official ACS Design Grant application platform.

APPLY NOW

Official programme and application page:
https://www.convergence.finance/accelerator/acs

Information session:
https://www.convergence.finance/calendar/3TJSC0ZOZnYpgy5kYMy3dP/view

Applicants should rely on the official Convergence website and application materials for the final requirements, documentation, terms, and any programme updates before submitting.

Why This Opportunity Matters for Climate Finance in Southeast Asia

The Asia Climate Solutions Design Grant addresses one of the most significant challenges facing climate action: transforming promising ideas and climate solutions into investable structures capable of attracting capital at meaningful scale.

Agriculture, food systems, forests, coastlines, watersheds, and natural ecosystems are deeply connected to economic development and community resilience across Southeast Asia. Yet investment gaps can prevent promising solutions from reaching the scale required.

By combining catalytic funding with technical assistance, investor connections, market knowledge, and blended finance expertise, the ACS Design Grant aims to help bridge the gap between early-stage financial innovation and commercially viable investment vehicles.

The emphasis on private capital mobilization is particularly significant. Rather than relying exclusively on grant funding to finance climate activities, the programme seeks to use catalytic resources to develop financial structures capable of attracting substantially larger pools of investment.

For organizations already developing innovative climate finance vehicles, the programme therefore offers an opportunity not only to secure funding for design and structuring but also to strengthen the foundations needed to reach investors and eventually achieve financial close.

Conclusion

The Asia Climate Solutions Design Grant 2026 offers a significant funding and acceleration opportunity for organizations developing innovative blended finance solutions addressing climate-resilient agriculture, food security, and nature-based solutions across Southeast Asia.

With Feasibility Study Grants of up to AUD 200,000 and Proof-of-Concept Grants of up to AUD 350,000, the programme can support organizations at different stages of developing their blended finance vehicles. Successful applicants can also benefit from Convergence’s technical expertise, investor and ecosystem networks, training, blended finance data, market insights, and peer-learning opportunities.

Strong proposals will need to demonstrate meaningful climate and development impact, intentional gender considerations, organizational capabilities, additionality, scalability, innovation, a credible pathway toward financial close, and strong stakeholder support.

Organizations do not have to be headquartered in the eligible Southeast Asian markets, but their proposed activities and end beneficiaries must target Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and/or Vietnam.

Interested organizations should carefully review the programme requirements, consider attending the September 10 information session, and begin preparing their concept notes well ahead of the September 28, 2026 at 9:00 PM ET / September 29, 2026 at 9:00 AM SGT deadline.

Visit the OFY website for more Grant Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The African Women in Agricultural Research and Development (AWARD) has opened applications for the 2026 Leadership Training Program for Emerging African Women in Agricultural Sciences. Funded by the Andrew Carnegie Foundation, formerly Carnegie Corporation of New York, the initiative is designed to strengthen the leadership capacity, confidence, professional visibility and influence of young African women working in agricultural sciences.

The nine-month program seeks to develop a cohort of at least 40 talented African women under the age of 35 and their mentors. Through intensive, non-residential training, participants will develop practical leadership and career skills while strengthening their ability to contribute to agricultural science, gender equality and broader agricultural development.

Opportunity Overview

  • Program: 2026 AWARD Leadership Training Program for Emerging African Women in Agricultural Sciences
  • Organiser: African Women in Agricultural Research and Development (AWARD)
  • Funding: Andrew Carnegie Foundation, formerly Carnegie Corporation of New York
  • Duration: Nine months
  • Format: Intensive, non-residential career transformation program
  • Target: At least 40 young African women under 35, selected competitively, together with their mentors
  • Application deadline: 20 September 2026 at midnight, East Africa Time (UTC+3)
  • Application method: Online application form
  • Eligible countries: Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Senegal, Tanzania and Zambia

About the AWARD Leadership Training Program

The AWARD Leadership Training Program is intended to invest in the potential of young African women working in agricultural sciences and help them become more competent, confident and influential professionals.

The program recognises that women working in agricultural science can face institutional and professional barriers that affect their career progression. It therefore focuses on building the leadership, communication, networking and strategic skills participants need to navigate these challenges and advance in their careers.

The initiative also promotes greater awareness of gender integration and gender equality in agriculture-related professions. Participants are expected to strengthen not only their individual careers but also their capacity to contribute to broader changes within agricultural research and development.

The selected participants will come from a range of disciplines within the biophysical and social sciences applied to agriculture. The program is also designed to reflect the diversity of African institutions and professional environments, including universities, research centres, government institutions, NGOs, civil society organisations and the private sector.

What Participants Will Gain

The program offers a broad professional and leadership development experience. Selected participants will have the opportunity to:

1. Strengthen leadership skills

Participants will explore different types of effective leadership and develop a stronger understanding of how leadership can be applied within professional and organisational settings.

The training is designed to help emerging women leaders become more confident in taking responsibility, influencing others and contributing meaningfully to their organisations and sectors.

2. Develop a strategic career path

Participants will learn how to define their career direction and make strategic use of professional networks to advance their careers.

This focus can help participants better understand where they want to go professionally and how relationships, collaborations and networks can contribute to achieving their long-term goals.

3. Build a strong personal brand

Another major component of the program is personal branding.

Participants will develop the confidence and practical skills required to communicate their expertise, ideas and achievements effectively. This includes preparing to present or propose promising ideas to funders, financing agencies and potential collaborators.

A stronger professional profile can help researchers and agricultural science professionals increase their visibility and make their work more accessible to potential partners and supporters.

4. Improve team management and organisational skills

The training will provide tools and skills for managing teams effectively.

Participants will explore how to understand organisational dynamics, develop alliances and make carefully considered decisions, including taking calculated risks when appropriate.

These skills are particularly relevant for emerging professionals who aspire to move into management, research leadership or other positions of responsibility.

5. Strengthen gender leadership and negotiation skills

The program also places significant emphasis on gender issues.

Participants will develop a better understanding of gender-related challenges and learn recognised strategies for addressing difficult situations. The training aims to help participants negotiate challenging circumstances and transform obstacles into opportunities for professional success.

6. Expand professional networks

The program brings together young women working across different agricultural science disciplines and professional environments.

This creates opportunities for participants to interact with professionals from universities, research institutions, government, NGOs, civil society and the private sector.

Such connections can contribute to future collaboration, knowledge exchange and professional development.

7. Increase research communication and professional visibility

The program is intended to help participants improve their ability to communicate their research and professional ideas to diverse audiences.

This is particularly valuable for agricultural scientists whose work may need to reach policymakers, funders, development organisations, industry representatives and communities beyond the academic environment.

Learn More HERE.

Who Can Apply?

The 2026 leadership training program specifically targets young African women under the age of 35 who are engaged in agricultural sciences.

Applicants should be working or involved in fields related to agricultural science, including disciplines within the biophysical and social sciences applied to agriculture.

The program can attract women working across different types of organisations, including:

  • Universities and higher education institutions
  • Research centres and research organisations
  • Government institutions
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • Civil society organisations
  • Private-sector organisations
  • Other institutions involved in agricultural research and development

Applicants are selected through a competitive process.

The source specifically identifies the target group as young African women under 35 working in agricultural sciences and lists the eligible countries. It does not provide additional detailed academic degree, employment-duration or nationality requirements in the supplied announcement; applicants should therefore consult the official application guidelines and FAQ before submitting an application.

Eligible Countries

For this particular 2026 call, applications are specifically targeted at women from the following 11 sub-Saharan African countries:

  1. Benin
  2. Burkina Faso
  3. Côte d’Ivoire
  4. Ethiopia
  5. Ghana
  6. Kenya
  7. Malawi
  8. Nigeria
  9. Senegal
  10. Tanzania
  11. Zambia

Therefore, applicants from other African countries should not assume that they are eligible for this particular edition simply because the program is described as an African initiative.

Program Structure and Duration

The selected participants will take part in an intensive, non-residential nine-month career transformation program.

The program will cover several interconnected areas of professional and leadership development, including:

  • Effective leadership
  • Career planning
  • Strategic networking
  • Personal branding
  • Professional confidence
  • Communicating ideas to funders and financing agencies
  • Team management
  • Organisational dynamics
  • Alliance building
  • Calculated risk-taking
  • Gender awareness
  • Negotiation
  • Managing difficult situations
  • Transforming professional challenges into opportunities

The program will also involve mentors alongside the selected participants, with the overall initiative planning to support at least 40 women and their mentors.

Application Requirements

Applicants should carefully review the official application instructions before beginning their submission.

The announcement makes clear that applications must be submitted exclusively through the online application form.

Applicants should also review the official FAQ because it provides additional information about the program and application process.

Important application documents

The official announcement provides links to:

  • Application submission instructions
  • Frequently Asked Questions
  • Online application form

Applicants should read the instructions carefully and make sure they understand the eligibility requirements and application procedure before submitting their application.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

20 September 2026 at midnight, East Africa Time (UTC+3).

No applications will be accepted after the stated deadline.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Preparing the required information early can help prevent technical or documentation problems close to the deadline.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should follow the official application instructions and submit their applications through the designated online form.

Application submission instructions: Download the official application guidelines

Frequently Asked Questions: Download the official FAQ

Online application form: Apply through the official online form

Applicants can also visit the Official AWARD Website for information about AWARD’s programs and training opportunities.

Why This Program Matters

Agriculture is closely connected to food security, livelihoods, environmental sustainability and economic development across Africa. Women working in agricultural research and development play an important role in addressing these challenges.

However, professional advancement can be affected by institutional barriers, limited access to leadership opportunities and unequal professional visibility.

The AWARD leadership training program seeks to address some of these challenges by combining leadership development, career planning, communication, networking, personal branding and gender-related training.

By supporting young women at an early stage of their professional careers, the program aims to help build a stronger pipeline of women leaders in agricultural science.

Tips for Applicants

Applicants should approach the application strategically rather than treating it as a routine training application.

1. Read the official instructions carefully

Before completing the application, study the application guidelines and FAQ. Pay particular attention to the eligibility requirements and instructions for submitting the application.

2. Clearly demonstrate your connection to agricultural science

Your application should make it easy for reviewers to understand how your academic, professional or research activities relate to agricultural sciences.

3. Highlight your leadership potential

Since this is a leadership-focused program, applicants should clearly demonstrate their existing leadership experiences, responsibilities, initiatives or potential for leadership.

4. Demonstrate your career ambitions

Explain how the program could contribute to your professional development and how you intend to use the knowledge, networks and skills gained through the training.

5. Pay attention to gender and agricultural development

The program places strong emphasis on gender integration and equality in agriculture. Applicants should therefore demonstrate an understanding of how their work or professional interests connect with broader agricultural and gender-related challenges where relevant.

6. Submit before the deadline

Do not wait until the final hours of 20 September 2026. Early submission provides additional time to address any issues with the online application.

About African Women in Agricultural Research and Development

African Women in Agricultural Research and Development, commonly known as AWARD, is the organisation behind the initiative.

The organisation focuses on supporting women working in agricultural research and development and strengthening their capacity to contribute to agricultural transformation.

The 2026 leadership training initiative is funded by the Andrew Carnegie Foundation, formerly known as Carnegie Corporation of New York.

AWARD is hosted by the World Agroforestry Centre, with its listed contact location in Nairobi, Kenya.

Visit HERE to learn more about the AWARD Leadership Program for Young African Women in Agricultural Sciences.

Conclusion

The 2026 AWARD Leadership Training Program for Emerging African Women in Agricultural Sciences presents an opportunity for young women in agricultural science to strengthen their leadership capabilities, expand professional networks and develop skills that can support long-term career advancement.

Through its nine-month non-residential structure, the program combines leadership development, career planning, personal branding, team management, networking, gender awareness and professional communication. It also seeks to strengthen the participation and influence of women in agricultural science and promote greater gender equality within agriculture-related professions.

Young African women under 35 working in agricultural sciences in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Senegal, Tanzania or Zambia should carefully review the official requirements and consider applying.

The deadline is 20 September 2026 at midnight East Africa Time (UTC+3), and applications must be submitted through the official online application form before the deadline.

Discover more global Fellowship and Leadership Development opportunities on OFY.

item.content:encoded:
The Technology Talent Services (TTS) Nigeria Programme is a free technology skills and workforce development initiative designed to equip young Nigerian women with practical, career-focused skills and strengthen their pathways into employment within Nigeria’s growing technology and Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) sector. Implemented by the Technology for Social Change and Development Initiative (Tech4Dev) with funding support from the Mastercard Foundation, the programme provides free application, training, and tech-enabled job placement opportunities for eligible women aged 18 to 35.

Running from February 2026 to July 2027, the 18-month initiative aims to help participants develop in-demand skills, improve their workforce readiness, and access career pathways across areas including software engineering, cybersecurity, Data and AI, full-stack development, virtual assistance, executive administrative support, and other technology-enabled roles.

About the Technology Talent Services (TTS) Nigeria Programme

The Technology Talent Services (TTS) Nigeria Programme is a workforce development initiative led by Tech4Dev and funded by the Mastercard Foundation.

The programme has been established within a broader effort to improve workforce participation, employment pathways, economic inclusion, and the development of Nigeria’s technology-enabled BPO sector.

TTS Nigeria will run for 18 months, beginning in February 2026 and concluding in July 2027.

Key programme information includes:

  • Programme Name: Technology Talent Services (TTS) Nigeria
  • Lead Implementing Organization: Technology for Social Change and Development Initiative (Tech4Dev)
  • Funding Partner: Mastercard Foundation
  • Programme Duration: February 2026 to July 2027
  • Duration: 18 months
  • Programme Location: 12 states in Nigeria
  • Programme Cost: Free
  • Target Applicants: Female Nigerian citizens aged 18–35

The programme’s approach goes beyond participation in training. Information collected throughout the initiative will help organizers monitor skills development, workforce readiness, employment outcomes, programme effectiveness, and opportunities to improve future workforce-development initiatives.

What Is the TTS Nigeria Programme Designed to Achieve?

TTS Nigeria is focused on helping create stronger workforce and employment pathways, particularly for young women.

The programme will collect and evaluate information relating to participation, skill development, workforce readiness, employment outcomes, and participant experiences. These insights will be used to improve programme delivery and understand how workforce-development interventions can contribute to greater economic participation.

The initiative is also connected to efforts to support the growth of Nigeria’s technology BPO sector.

Among the areas the programme intends to monitor and strengthen are:

  1. Programme participation and completion.
  2. Participants’ development of relevant skills.
  3. Workforce readiness.
  4. Employment and placement outcomes.
  5. Employer alignment.
  6. Economic inclusion.
  7. Employment pathways for young Nigerians.
  8. Opportunities for women and underserved groups.
  9. The development of Nigeria’s technology BPO workforce.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to young Nigerian women interested in improving their skills and positioning themselves for future workforce opportunities.

Who Can Apply for the TTS Nigeria Programme?

The initial eligibility requirements are clearly defined.

To proceed with an application, an individual must be:

  • Female
  • Between 18 and 35 years old
  • A Nigerian citizen

Applicants are required to complete an initial eligibility screening before they are asked to provide additional personal and contact information.

If an applicant’s answers do not meet any of these basic eligibility requirements, the applicant will not be able to continue to the full application.

This initial screening process is intended to avoid unnecessarily collecting additional personal information from individuals who do not qualify for the programme.

Applicants should therefore carefully confirm their eligibility before starting the application.

Why the Eligibility Check Comes Before the Full Application

TTS Nigeria has structured its application process so that applicants first answer a small number of basic eligibility questions.

These include questions relating to:

  • Gender
  • Nationality
  • Age

Only applicants who meet the programme’s fundamental eligibility criteria can proceed to the next stage.

According to the programme information, this process has been established to protect applicants’ data and time. More detailed information, including names and contact information, is requested only after the basic eligibility requirements have been confirmed.

Applicants must provide accurate information throughout the process. Providing false or misleading information may result in disqualification at any stage of the application or selection process.

The TTS Nigeria Programme Is Free

One of the most important details prospective applicants should know is that the TTS Nigeria Programme is free.

Eligible applicants should therefore not interpret the programme as requiring tuition or a participation fee based on the information provided in the official registration form.

Applicants should also remember that submitting an application does not automatically guarantee selection.

The registration form is described as the first step in applying to the programme. Applications and responses will be used to understand each applicant’s background, training needs, and suitability for available opportunities.

Training, Skills and Workforce Development

TTS Nigeria is structured around skills and workforce development, with programme monitoring covering areas such as specialization tracks, skill assessments, workforce readiness, employer alignment, and employment outcomes.

Participants may have information recorded relating to:

  • Their training cohort
  • Their specialization track
  • Attendance
  • Skill-assessment outcomes
  • Workforce-readiness indicators
  • Employer-alignment assessments
  • Employment status
  • Placement outcomes

This demonstrates the programme’s strong focus on the relationship between training and participants’ eventual workforce outcomes.

Rather than considering training as an isolated activity, TTS Nigeria aims to understand how participants progress through the programme and how their skills can translate into stronger employment pathways.

Employment Matching and Placement Opportunities

Another important component of the programme is its connection with BPO partner firms, employers and hiring partners.

The programme information indicates that participant data may eventually be shared with BPO partner firms for employment matching and placement purposes, subject to additional explicit consent from participants at the placement stage.

This employment-oriented component is significant because the initiative is designed not only to develop skills but also to contribute to workforce participation and employment pathways.

Participants should, however, understand that the available programme information does not guarantee that every individual who completes the programme will automatically receive employment.

Focus on Women and Inclusive Economic Opportunities

TTS Nigeria places particular emphasis on creating opportunities for young women.

The programme also recognizes the importance of improving opportunities for groups that may experience additional barriers to economic participation.

Information provided in the programme’s consent documentation specifically refers to creating more opportunities for:

  • Young women
  • Persons with disabilities
  • Internally displaced persons

Where applicable, participants may be asked about disability or Internally Displaced Person (IDP) status so that programme organizers can understand participant circumstances and support inclusive programme delivery.

However, the fundamental eligibility criteria remain that applicants must be female Nigerian citizens between 18 and 35 years old.

Programme Locations

TTS Nigeria is scheduled to operate across 12 states in Nigeria.

The registration information provided does not list the names of all 12 states. Applicants should therefore rely on the official TTS Nigeria application platform and programme communications for confirmation of participating states, training locations, and any location-specific requirements.

Applicants may be asked to provide their:

  • State of residence
  • Local government area of residence
  • Residential information

These details may help organizers understand participant distribution and manage programme delivery across the participating locations.

What Information May Applicants and Participants Be Asked to Provide?

Applicants who successfully pass the basic eligibility stage may be required to provide further personal, educational, professional, and programme-related information.

TTS Nigeria indicates that it may collect some or all of the following information:

  1. Full name and age.
  2. Gender.
  3. Phone number and email address.
  4. Residential address.
  5. State of residence.
  6. Local government area of residence.
  7. Training cohort information.
  8. Specialization track.
  9. Attendance records.
  10. Marital status.
  11. Disability status, where applicable.
  12. Internally Displaced Person status, where applicable.
  13. Educational background.
  14. Previous work experience.
  15. Skill-assessment results.
  16. Workforce-readiness indicators.
  17. Employer-alignment assessments.
  18. Employment status.
  19. Placement outcomes.
  20. Feedback and survey responses.
  21. Photographs or video recordings from programme activities, with separate consent where required.

Applicants should carefully read the programme’s consent and privacy information before submitting personal information.

Why Does TTS Nigeria Collect Participant Information?

According to the programme, participant information is collected to help Tech4Dev and its partners understand programme participation and outcomes while improving delivery.

The information may be used for purposes including:

  • Tracking participation and completion rates.
  • Assessing participants’ skill development.
  • Understanding employment outcomes.
  • Monitoring and evaluating programme effectiveness.
  • Improving programme design and delivery.
  • Supporting participant success.
  • Reporting programme progress and impact to the Mastercard Foundation.
  • Conducting research relating to workforce participation.
  • Studying employment pathways.
  • Understanding economic inclusion.
  • Supporting research relating to the growth of Nigeria’s technology BPO sector.

The programme states that information identifying participants will not be shared without permission except where required by law or programme safeguarding requirements.

Data Sharing and Programme Partners

TTS Nigeria explains that participant data may be shared with relevant organizations involved in programme implementation, evaluation and employment support.

Depending on consent and the purpose involved, these may include:

  • Mastercard Foundation, the programme’s funding partner.
  • Other implementing partners involved in similar Mastercard Foundation programmes.
  • Third-party data processors working with the Mastercard Foundation for monitoring and evaluation.
  • Third-party processors legitimately engaged by Tech4Dev for programme implementation with the necessary Mastercard Foundation approval.
  • BPO employers and hiring partners for employment matching and placement, subject to additional explicit participant consent at the placement stage.

Applicants are encouraged to read the relevant privacy policies before deciding whether to provide consent for data sharing.

Giving Consent Is Separate From Programme Participation

An important feature of the TTS Nigeria application process is the distinction between programme participation and consent to data sharing.

According to the consent information, applicants are not obligated to provide consent to data sharing in order to participate in the programme.

The programme states that a participant’s decision regarding data sharing will not affect their eligibility to participate in the programme.

Applicants therefore have a choice regarding whether they agree to share their data with TTS Nigeria, Mastercard Foundation, and relevant third-party data processors for the purposes described in the consent documentation.

Applicants should carefully read the consent statement before selecting their preferred option.

Participants’ Data Rights

TTS Nigeria outlines several rights participants have regarding their personal information.

These include:

Right to Access

Participants can request a copy of the personal information held about them.

Right to Rectification

Participants can ask for inaccurate information to be corrected.

Right to Erasure

Participants may request deletion of their information.

Right to Restriction of Processing

Participants can request restrictions on how their information is processed.

Right to Object to Processing

Participants can object to certain processing of their information.

Right to Data Portability

Participants can request that their data be transferred to another organization where applicable.

These rights are particularly important for applicants who want greater control over how their personal information is handled throughout the programme.

Can Participants Withdraw Their Consent?

Yes.

Participants who initially consent to sharing their information can withdraw that consent later.

The programme states that withdrawing consent will not affect an individual’s ability to participate in TTS Nigeria.

Participants wishing to withdraw consent can contact the TTS Nigeria Data Protection Officer through the contact information supplied by the programme.

Email: monitoring@ttsnigeria.org
Phone: +2347068556072

Applicants should retain relevant programme documentation and consent information for their records.

Why Participant Data Matters to the Programme

TTS Nigeria explains that participant information can help the programme better understand whether its interventions are achieving their intended objectives.

Data and participant feedback can help the programme:

  1. Demonstrate programme impact to funders and stakeholders.
  2. Improve programme design.
  3. Strengthen workforce-readiness support.
  4. Improve the participant experience.
  5. Support advocacy around youth employment.
  6. Generate insights into Nigeria’s technology BPO sector.
  7. Support the development of additional opportunities for young women.
  8. Improve inclusion for persons with disabilities and internally displaced persons.

Applicants should nevertheless make their own informed decision regarding consent after reviewing the programme’s privacy information.

How to Apply for the TTS Nigeria Programme

Eligible candidates interested in participating should complete the official TTS Nigeria Programme Registration Form.

The application begins with basic programme information, consent information, and an eligibility screening.

The general process is:

  1. Access the official TTS Nigeria registration form.
  2. Read the programme information carefully before beginning.
  3. Review the participant consent and data-protection information.
  4. Indicate your decision regarding data-sharing consent.
  5. Confirm that you understand the eligibility requirements.
  6. Complete the initial eligibility screening.
  7. Confirm that you are female.
  8. Confirm that you are a Nigerian citizen.
  9. Confirm that you fall within the required age range of 18–35.
  10. If eligible, proceed to the full application.
  11. Provide the requested information accurately and honestly.
  12. Review your responses before submitting the form.

Applicants should remember that completion of the application does not guarantee admission or selection into the programme.

The application is the first stage through which TTS Nigeria can assess applicants’ backgrounds, training needs, and suitability for available opportunities.

Important Information Before Applying

Prospective applicants should keep several important points in mind.

First, the programme is free, so applicants should be cautious about any unofficial individual or platform requesting payment in exchange for programme admission.

Second, applicants must provide accurate information. False information can lead to disqualification during the application or selection process.

Third, only female Nigerian citizens aged 18–35 meet the stated basic eligibility requirements.

Fourth, completing the registration form does not guarantee selection.

Finally, applicants should carefully review all consent and privacy information before providing personal information.

Application Deadline

No specific application deadline is stated in the programme registration information provided.

Prospective applicants are therefore encouraged to complete their applications as early as possible and check the official TTS Nigeria platform for any subsequently announced deadline, cohort timelines, or application updates.

The overall programme runs from February 2026 to July 2027.

APPLY NOW

About Tech4Dev

The Technology for Social Change and Development Initiative (Tech4Dev) is the lead implementing organization for the Technology Talent Services Nigeria Programme.

Through TTS Nigeria, the organization is working with the Mastercard Foundation to support skills development, workforce participation, employment pathways, and economic inclusion, particularly for young Nigerian women.

The programme also seeks to generate insights that can strengthen workforce-development initiatives and contribute to the growth of Nigeria’s technology BPO sector.

About the Mastercard Foundation’s Role

The Mastercard Foundation is identified as the funding partner for the TTS Nigeria Programme.

Programme monitoring and evaluation information may be used to report progress and impact to the Foundation and to generate broader insights into workforce development, economic inclusion, and employment pathways.

Applicants should consult the respective privacy policies of Tech4Dev/TTS Nigeria and the Mastercard Foundation for further information about personal-data processing.

Conclusion

The TTS Nigeria Programme 2026–2027 presents an important skills and workforce-development opportunity for young Nigerian women interested in strengthening their capabilities and positioning themselves for employment opportunities within a changing technology-driven economy.

Implemented by the Technology for Social Change and Development Initiative (Tech4Dev) and funded by the Mastercard Foundation, the free 18-month programme will operate across 12 Nigerian states between February 2026 and July 2027.

With an emphasis on skills development, workforce readiness, employment pathways, economic inclusion, and Nigeria’s growing technology BPO sector, TTS Nigeria is designed to help participants move beyond training toward stronger workforce participation.

To meet the basic eligibility requirements, applicants must be female Nigerian citizens between 18 and 35 years old. Candidates who satisfy these requirements can proceed through the eligibility screening and complete the full programme application.

Because no specific application deadline is included in the registration information provided, interested and eligible candidates should apply as early as possible and continue checking official TTS Nigeria communications for application deadlines, cohort information, participating locations, and other programme updates.

Applicants should also remember that registration does not guarantee selection and that all information submitted during the application process should be complete, accurate, and truthful.

Visit the OFY website for more Training Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The World Affairs Councils of America (WACA) Student Scholars Program 2026 offers undergraduate students an exceptional opportunity to gain firsthand exposure to careers in international affairs, global policy, diplomacy, and world affairs. The program is designed to create pathways into careers in world affairs while encouraging students to develop a lifelong interest in international issues. Through the program, 25 undergraduate students from WACA Council communities will be selected to attend the WACA National Conference at no cost. In addition to conference participation, WACA supports the costs associated with students’ travel, room, and board, giving selected scholars the opportunity to participate in a major national gathering without having to carry the full financial burden themselves. The program also includes Scholar Day, an exclusive Washington, DC experience that allows participating students to explore the world of international affairs beyond the conference itself. Students can visit think tanks, embassies, international organizations, and other institutions connected to global affairs. For students considering careers in diplomacy, international relations, public policy, government, international development, economics, security, nonprofit organizations, journalism, or related fields, the WACA Student Scholars Program can provide valuable exposure, professional connections, and a clearer understanding of possible career pathways.

About the WACA Student Scholars Program

The Student Scholars Program was established in 2010 with generous support from the Malú and Carlos Alvarez Family. Since its creation, the initiative has focused on connecting undergraduate students with the broader world affairs community and helping them explore educational and professional opportunities related to international affairs. The program is built around the idea that meaningful exposure to world affairs can help students make informed decisions about their academic and professional futures.

Rather than limiting participation to classroom learning, WACA provides scholars with opportunities to interact with institutions, professionals, and other students who share an interest in global issues.

The program therefore combines:

  • National conference participation
  • Professional and educational exposure
  • Washington, DC institutional visits
  • Networking opportunities
  • Career exploration
  • International affairs education
  • Engagement with the WACA Council network

What Does the Student Scholars Program Offer?

Selected scholars receive substantial support to participate in the WACA National Conference and related activities.

1. Attendance at the National Conference

WACA selects 25 undergraduate students from Council communities to participate in the National Conference.

The selected students attend the conference at no cost, allowing them to engage with the program without paying the standard conference participation costs.

The National Conference brings students into an environment focused on world affairs and provides opportunities to learn from people working across the international affairs field.

2. Travel and Lodging Support

WACA provides $1,250 to the nominating Council to help defray the Scholar’s travel and lodging expenses.

The funding is intended to help cover:

  • Travel-related costs
  • Lodging expenses
  • Double-occupancy accommodation

The participating Council is responsible for arranging the student’s transportation and hotel reservations.

Importantly, hotel arrangements must cover attendance for all three days of the National Conference.

WACA also helps Councils identify potential roommates by sharing the list of accepted Scholars with sponsoring Councils.

3. Scholar Day in Washington, DC

One of the distinctive elements of the program is Scholar Day, an exclusive excursion designed specifically for Student Scholars.

During this experience, students have the opportunity to explore Washington, DC institutions connected to international affairs.

Potential visits include:

  • Think tanks
  • Embassies
  • International organizations
  • Other institutions involved in global affairs and policy

This experience can help students move beyond theoretical classroom discussions and see how international affairs operates in professional and institutional settings.

4. Career and Academic Exploration

The program is designed to help students “map their global futures.”

By meeting professionals and visiting organizations involved in international affairs, students can gain a better understanding of potential career directions.

The experience may be particularly valuable for students interested in areas such as:

  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • Foreign policy
  • Global development
  • International economics
  • Public policy
  • Government
  • International organizations
  • Nonprofit and civil society work
  • Global security
  • International journalism
  • Research and think tanks

2026 Student Scholars Program Eligibility

The WACA Student Scholars Program has specific eligibility requirements.

Each participating Council may nominate one undergraduate student who is at least 18 years old and attends a local college or university.

Basic eligibility requirements

Applicants must:

  1. Be an undergraduate student.
  2. Be at least 18 years old.
  3. Attend a local college or university within an eligible WACA Council community.
  4. Be selected and nominated by their local WACA Council.
  5. Complete the national application process after being informed that they are the Council’s local nominee.

A critical point for prospective applicants is that students cannot simply submit an application independently and expect WACA to forward it to a local Council.

The Council first conducts its own local selection process. Once a student has been selected as the Council’s nominee, that student can proceed with the national application.

Who Is Not Eligible?

WACA specifically excludes several categories of students from consideration.

The following are not eligible:

  • High school students
  • Graduate students
  • College students in Greater Washington, DC (the DMV)
  • Prior nominees who were not selected

Therefore, students who are currently pursuing graduate-level studies should not apply, even if they previously participated in an undergraduate program.

Similarly, high school students are not eligible for this particular opportunity.

How Does the Nomination Process Work?

The WACA Student Scholars Program uses a two-stage nomination and application process.

Understanding this process is extremely important because students cannot bypass the local Council selection stage.

Stage 1: Local Council Selection

The local WACA Council identifies and selects its Student Scholar nominee.

Each Council can nominate only one undergraduate student.

Multiple nominees from the same Council will not be considered.

WACA encourages local Councils to promote the opportunity broadly among nearby colleges and universities so that students who may not already be heavily involved with the Council can learn about the program.

Among applicants who are equally qualified and show promise, preference is given to nominees who may not yet have significant local Council involvement.

This means that students should not assume they are at a disadvantage simply because they have not previously been deeply involved with their local World Affairs Council.

Stage 2: National Application

After the local Council has selected its nominee, the nominated student must complete the national application process.

The Council and the student have separate submission requirements.

Documents Required From the Nominating Council

Once a nominee has been selected, the Council must submit:

1. Online Council Nomination Form

The nominating Council must complete the official online nomination form.

2. Professor’s Letter of Recommendation

The Council must also submit a letter of recommendation from a professor of the nominated student.

The student is responsible for making sure that the professor sends the recommendation to the Council in sufficient time for the Council to submit the complete nomination.

Students should therefore contact their professor well before the deadline rather than waiting until the final days.

Documents Required From the Nominated Student

After being selected as the Council’s nominee, the student must submit:

1. Online Student Application Form

The nominated student must complete WACA’s official Student Application Form.

2. Current Resume

Applicants must provide an up-to-date resume highlighting their education, experience, activities, achievements, interests, and other relevant qualifications.

3. Letter of Intent

Applicants must submit a 1–2 page Letter of Intent.

This document provides the student with an opportunity to explain their interests, goals, aspirations, and reasons for wanting to participate in the Student Scholars Program.

Applicants should use the Letter of Intent strategically to demonstrate how participation could contribute to their academic development, professional goals, and interest in world affairs.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2026 WACA Student Scholars Program is Friday, September 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT. Prospective students should not wait until the deadline to begin preparing their documents. Because the process involves local Council selection, a professor’s recommendation, a Council nomination, and the student’s national application, students should begin by contacting their local WACA Council and asking about its internal selection timeline.

What Happens After Applications Are Submitted?

After applications are submitted, nominated students are reviewed by the WACA national office in consultation with the WACA Board of Directors.

The final selections are expected to be announced within two weeks after the application deadline.

Selected students then participate in the National Conference and associated Student Scholar activities.

To apply click HERE: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSftagIkRIxSyVp09lPabc4PF4U39lLTGznFdHhH4Yhec4PXZw/viewform

Student Scholar Participation Requirements

Selection for the program comes with responsibilities.

As part of their participation requirements, Student Scholars must submit:

  • A brief evaluation of their experience
  • A report about their experience

These materials must be submitted no later than two weeks after the National Conference.

This requirement allows WACA to collect feedback from participating students and better understand the value and impact of the Student Scholars experience.

Why Should Undergraduate Students Consider This Opportunity?

The WACA Student Scholars Program offers more than attendance at a conference.

For an undergraduate student interested in global affairs, the experience can provide exposure to people and institutions that may otherwise be difficult to access at the undergraduate level.

Exposure to the World Affairs Community

Students gain an opportunity to become more familiar with the organizations and professionals shaping conversations around international affairs.

Washington, DC Experience

Scholar Day provides students with an opportunity to visit institutions in Washington, DC and gain firsthand insight into the work conducted by think tanks, embassies, international organizations, and other institutions.

Career Exploration

Students can use the experience to investigate potential career paths and better understand how their academic interests connect with professional opportunities.

Networking

Participating alongside other Student Scholars and engaging with the wider WACA community can help students develop relationships that may remain valuable beyond the program.

Professional Development

Preparing a resume, writing a Letter of Intent, communicating with professors, working with a Council, and participating in a national program can all contribute to professional development.

Global Perspective

The program encourages students to think beyond their local academic environment and engage with broader international questions and institutions.

An Important Point About Local Council Selection

One of the most important details applicants should understand is that the Student Application Form is not a substitute for local Council selection.

WACA explicitly explains that the national forms are not intended for local selection and that submissions will not be forwarded to Councils for their own selection process.

Councils must conduct their own local selection and collect the necessary documents.

Therefore, students should:

  1. Identify the WACA Council connected to their local community.
  2. Contact the Council to ask about its Student Scholars selection process.
  3. Follow the Council’s local nomination requirements.
  4. Wait until the Council informs them that they are the selected local nominee.
  5. Complete the national Student Application Form after receiving that confirmation.
  6. Submit the required resume and Letter of Intent.
  7. Ensure that the professor’s recommendation reaches the Council on time.

This process is particularly important because only one student can be nominated by each Council.

Additional links for info here: https://worldaffairscouncils.org/student-scholars-program/

Official Program Resources and Application Links

Students and Councils can access the official WACA resources below:

Students should verify all requirements and deadlines through the official WACA materials before submitting their application.

For more info/ inquiry here:waca@worldaffairscouncils.org

Tips for Prospective Student Scholars

Start With Your Local Council

Do not begin by completing the national application form. First determine which WACA Council serves your area and ask about its local nomination process.

Prepare Your Resume Early

Make sure your resume is current and clearly presents your education, extracurricular activities, leadership experience, research, volunteer work, internships, awards, and relevant interests.

Give Your Professor Enough Time

The recommendation letter is an important part of the nomination process. Contact your professor early and clearly communicate the Council’s deadline.

Make Your Letter of Intent Personal

The Letter of Intent should explain why you are interested in world affairs and how the Student Scholars experience connects with your academic and career goals.

Do Not Assume Previous Council Involvement Is Required

WACA indicates that, among equally qualified applicants of promise, preference may be given to students who do not yet have significant local Council involvement.

Students should therefore consider applying even if they have not previously been highly active in their local Council.

Confirm the Deadline and Time Zone

The final national application deadline is September 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT. Applicants should submit their materials before the final hours to avoid technical or document-related problems.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many students will be selected?

WACA offers the opportunity to 25 undergraduate students from Council communities.

Is participation in the National Conference free?

Yes. Selected Student Scholars attend the National Conference at no cost.

Does WACA provide travel and lodging support?

WACA provides $1,250 to the nominating Council to help defray the Scholar’s travel and lodging costs, including double-occupancy accommodation.

Who arranges transportation and hotel reservations?

The participating Council is responsible for arranging transportation and hotel reservations for its Scholar.

Can two students from the same Council be nominated?

No. Each Council may nominate one undergraduate student, and multiple nominees from the same Council will not be considered.

Can graduate students apply?

No. Graduate students are specifically excluded from eligibility.

Can high school students apply?

No. The program is intended for undergraduate students who are at least 18 years old.

Can students in the DMV apply?

No. College students in Greater Washington, DC, commonly referred to as the DMV, are not eligible.

Can a student who was nominated in the past but not selected apply again?

No. Prior nominees who were not selected are listed among those who are not eligible.

Does the program have a nationality restriction?

The provided eligibility requirements do not identify a specific nationality, race, or continental restriction. Eligibility is primarily tied to undergraduate status, age, attendance at an eligible local institution, and nomination through a WACA Council.

When will the results be announced?

WACA states that selections will be announced within two weeks after the application deadline.

Conclusion

The WACA Student Scholars Program 2026 provides undergraduate students with an opportunity to gain meaningful exposure to the world affairs community while participating in the WACA National Conference and an exclusive Scholar Day experience in Washington, DC. With support for conference participation and financial assistance provided through the nominating Council for travel and lodging, the program can give selected students access to professional environments, international organizations, think tanks, embassies, and other institutions that can help shape their understanding of global affairs. The program is particularly valuable for undergraduate students who are beginning to consider careers related to international relations, diplomacy, public policy, government, international development, global economics, research, and other world affairs fields. However, prospective applicants should remember that this is a Council-based nomination program. Students cannot simply submit the national application independently. They must first be selected as the nominee of their local WACA Council. Eligible undergraduate students should therefore begin by contacting their local Council, learning about its internal nomination process, preparing their resume and Letter of Intent, and arranging their professor recommendation well ahead of the final deadline.
