item.content:encoded:
The Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) is inviting applications for its Internship at the Inter-Parliamentary Union, offering an opportunity for individuals interested in parliamentary affairs, international relations, democracy, political institutions, administration, human rights, development and multilateral cooperation to gain professional experience within the world organization of national parliaments.

Based at the IPU Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, the internship is offered for one year and provides a monthly stipend of CHF 1,500 for a full-time 37.5-hour working week. Depending on the service or division to which an intern is assigned, some alternative working arrangements, including telecommuting, may be available.

The application deadline is 3 September 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time (CET).

About the Inter-Parliamentary Union Internship

The Inter-Parliamentary Union is the world organization of national parliaments and dates back to 1889, making it the oldest political multilateral organization in the world.

The organization works to promote the peaceful settlement of conflicts through political dialogue and negotiation. Its broader mission is to contribute to stronger parliaments and better democracies.

The IPU currently has 183 Member Parliaments, while its Secretariat carries out the organization’s day-to-day work. The Secretariat is based primarily at the IPU Headquarters in Geneva and supports Member Parliaments in strengthening their institutions and delivering on the organization’s policy priorities.

Interns work within this international and multicultural environment, supporting the Secretariat’s different services and divisions.

The IPU’s work covers areas including:

  • External relations with Member Parliaments
  • Technical cooperation
  • Resource Centre activities
  • Gender partnership
  • Youth empowerment
  • International development
  • Human rights
  • Communications
  • Support services
  • Executive Office functions

This makes the internship potentially valuable for individuals seeking experience in international organizations, parliamentary institutions, public policy, international development and multilateral affairs.

Internship Responsibilities

The selected intern will work under the authority of a manager and support the administrative and substantive functions of the relevant service or division.

Responsibilities may include the following:

1. Supporting meetings and activities

The intern may assist with the logistical preparation of activities and meetings. This can include helping prepare documentation, materials and other resources required for successful meetings and events.

2. Supporting correspondence and workflows

The intern will provide administrative support for correspondence coming into and leaving the relevant division or team.

This includes helping ensure that workflows and processes are properly aligned and that correspondence is handled efficiently.

3. Maintaining records and spreadsheets

The position involves maintaining spreadsheets and correspondence records. This provides practical exposure to administrative systems and organizational record management.

4. Supporting communications from the Secretary General

The intern may assist with processing communications that require the signature of the IPU Secretary General.

This responsibility requires attention to detail, professionalism and discretion.

5. Attending meetings and preparing minutes

The intern may attend meetings, including meetings involving the IPU President and Secretary General when required.

Where assigned, the intern will help prepare concise minutes that focus particularly on:

  • Key meeting outcomes
  • Decisions
  • Follow-up actions
  • Relevant responsibilities

6. Supporting IPU activities and assemblies

The intern may provide general support during IPU activities, meetings, biannual assemblies and other ad hoc events.

This can offer exposure to the practical organization of high-level international and parliamentary activities.

7. Conducting research

The intern may also undertake research connected to the specific activities or programmes of the service or division where they are placed.

The exact workflow and responsibilities will depend on the schedule of meetings, missions and activities within the assigned team.

The intern may also be required to perform other duties considered appropriate by their manager.

Working Environment and Confidentiality

Because the IPU handles sensitive matters, the selected intern will be expected to demonstrate a high level of discretion and respect for confidentiality.

The organization operates in an international and multicultural environment. Applicants should therefore be prepared to work professionally with colleagues from different cultural and professional backgrounds.

Strong communication skills are particularly important because the IPU has two official languages: English and French.

Candidates should be able to communicate both orally and in writing in English and French. Knowledge of additional languages is considered an asset.

Location, Duration and Working Hours

The internship is based at the IPU Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.

Key details include:

  • Location: Geneva, Switzerland
  • Working arrangement: 100% at IPU Headquarters, although telecommuting or other arrangements may be possible depending on the assigned service or division
  • Duration: One year
  • Working week: 37.5 hours
  • Contract: 100% internship
  • Monthly stipend: CHF 1,500

The possibility of telecommuting is not presented as a universal arrangement. It depends on the service or division in which the intern is placed.

Internship Stipend

The IPU will provide the selected intern with a monthly stipend of CHF 1,500 for a 100% contract based on a 37.5-hour working week.

This makes the opportunity a paid internship rather than an unpaid placement.

Applicants should nevertheless carefully consider the cost of living and other expenses associated with living and working in Geneva, as the source information only specifies the monthly stipend and does not state that accommodation, travel, visa or relocation expenses are separately covered.

Who Should Apply?

The internship is intended for candidates who are interested in gaining experience within an international parliamentary and multilateral organization.

The IPU states that its personnel are expected to demonstrate:

  • Motivation and a strong commitment to the organization’s principles
  • The ability to work effectively in a multicultural team
  • A high level of technical knowledge relevant to the position
  • Work experience at national and/or international level
  • Fluency in at least one of the IPU’s official languages, English or French
  • Working knowledge of a second official language
  • Additional language skills as an advantage

The source does not specify a particular academic degree, field of study, minimum age or nationality requirement for this internship. Applicants should therefore focus on demonstrating relevant knowledge, skills, experience, language ability and motivation.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to submit several pieces of information as part of their application.

1. Curriculum vitae

Candidates should provide an up-to-date CV outlining their education, professional experience, relevant skills, language abilities and other information demonstrating their suitability for the internship.

2. Brief motivation statement

Applicants must provide a brief explanation of no more than 200 words describing why they are the right person for the internship.

This is an important opportunity to demonstrate motivation, relevant experience and an understanding of the IPU’s work.

3. Availability

Applicants must provide information about their availability to begin the internship.

Candidates should therefore clearly indicate when they would be able to take up the position.

4. Swiss residence or work permit status

Applicants must also provide information about their current Swiss resident/work permit status.

Candidates should ensure that this information is accurate and up to date when submitting their application.

How to Apply

Applications should be submitted by email to the IPU.

Candidates should send their application to job@ipu.org and use “Internship” as the subject line.

For general information about the internship, candidates can contact postbox@ipu.org.

Official IPU Internship Information and Application Page

Applicants should ensure that their submissions are complete and arrive before the stated deadline.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is:

3 September 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time (CET).

Incomplete applications and applications submitted after the deadline will not be accepted.

Candidates should also note that the IPU states that only applicants under serious consideration will be contacted.

The IPU also gives particular attention to candidates from developing countries and to achieving gender balance.

The organization’s recruitment principles emphasize the importance of:

  • Professional competence
  • Integrity
  • Motivation
  • Commitment to IPU principles
  • Multicultural teamwork
  • Relevant technical knowledge
  • National and/or international work experience
  • English and French language skills

Why This Internship Could Be Valuable

An internship with the Inter-Parliamentary Union can provide practical exposure to the functioning of an international multilateral organization working directly with national parliaments.

Depending on the assigned division, interns may gain experience in areas such as:

  • International parliamentary affairs
  • Democracy and governance
  • Political dialogue
  • International development
  • Human rights
  • Gender equality

Professional Skills You Can Develop

Research skills

Communication skills

Meeting and reporting skills

Preparing concise minutes focused on outcomes and follow-up actions can provide valuable experience in professional reporting and documentation.

Multicultural teamwork

The IPU operates in an international environment, giving interns the opportunity to collaborate with people from different professional and cultural backgrounds.

Confidentiality and professional judgment

Because the organization deals with sensitive issues, interns are expected to demonstrate discretion and protect confidential information.

International and Multicultural Environment

The IPU’s Secretariat is designed to support national parliaments around the world. Its work therefore takes place within an international context involving diverse institutions, countries and perspectives.

The organization emphasizes its commitment to diversity and an environment in which individual contributions are valued.

The IPU also highlights the importance of gender equality in its employment practices.

For candidates interested in international careers, this multicultural environment can provide exposure to how a global organization coordinates its work across different national and institutional contexts.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully consider the following:

  1. Check the deadline carefully. Applications must arrive by 23:59 CET on 3 September 2026.
  2. Prepare a focused CV. Highlight experience and skills that are relevant to the internship.
  3. Keep the motivation statement within 200 words. The statement should clearly explain why you are suitable for the role.
  4. Explain your availability clearly. State when you could begin the internship.
  5. Provide your Swiss residence/work permit status. Make sure the information is accurate.
  6. Highlight your language skills. English and French are the IPU’s official languages, and knowledge of both is expected.
  7. Demonstrate multicultural teamwork. Relevant national or international experience can strengthen your application.
  8. Show professionalism and discretion. These qualities are particularly important given the sensitive nature of the IPU’s work.
  9. Submit a complete application. The IPU states that incomplete applications will not be accepted.
  10. Apply before the deadline. Late applications will not be considered.

Conclusion

The IPU Internship in Geneva provides an opportunity to gain practical experience within one of the world’s leading multilateral parliamentary organizations. With a one-year duration, a CHF 1,500 monthly stipend, and the possibility of working alongside professionals supporting national parliaments across the world, the opportunity may be particularly relevant to individuals seeking to build experience in international organizations, governance, diplomacy, public policy, parliamentary affairs, human rights, development, research or related fields.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Iceland is accepting applications for a full-time doctoral research position examining water governance in low-income African countries. The three-year project will investigate how rural water-governance systems can be made more sustainable, efficient and equitable, with a particular focus on Uganda, Malawi and Sierra Leone.

The selected doctoral researcher will join the University’s interdisciplinary Environment and Natural Resources programme and work with experts in resource management, development studies, economics, social sciences and water governance.

The project is funded by the Icelandic Ministry for Foreign Affairs through the University of Iceland PhD Grants Fund. It combines academic research, policy analysis, development cooperation and field-based data collection.

The expected starting date is 1 November 2026 or another date agreed with the University. Applications must be submitted by 4 September 2026.

Interested candidates should review the EURAXESS listing and the official University of Iceland vacancy notice before applying.

PhD Position at a Glance

Key information Details
Host institution University of Iceland
Location Reykjavík, Iceland
Research project Water Governance in Low-Income African Countries
Programme Environment and Natural Resources
Position type Full-time doctoral research position
Funding source Icelandic Ministry for Foreign Affairs through the University of Iceland PhD Grants Fund
Funding period Three years
Primary geographic focus Uganda, Malawi and Sierra Leone
Main fieldwork focus Uganda
Research areas Water governance, resource management, development studies, policy analysis, social sciences and rural development
Expected starting date 1 November 2026 or by agreement
Application language Icelandic or English
Application deadline 4 September 2026
Contact person Jón Geir Pétursson
Contact email jgp@hi.is
EURAXESS reference 460279

About the Research Project

The project, titled “Water Governance in Low-Income African Countries,” seeks to advance knowledge of how water resources are governed, particularly in rural communities where public institutions, households and economic activities may face significant difficulties obtaining reliable access to safe water.

The project will examine the policies, institutions, governance arrangements and decision-making systems that influence water access, water quality, infrastructure management and the long-term sustainability of rural water services.

Water-governance challenges cannot be addressed through infrastructure alone. Even where wells, pumps, pipes, treatment facilities or storage systems exist, long-term service delivery may be undermined by weak institutional coordination, inadequate maintenance, limited financing, unclear responsibilities, unequal access or insufficient community participation.

The doctoral research will therefore examine water as both a natural resource and a public-governance issue.

Why Water Governance Matters

Water is essential for life, public health, food security and economic development. Reliable access to sufficient quantities of clean water is necessary for drinking, cooking, hygiene and sanitation.

Water also supports:

  • Agricultural production;
  • Livestock and rural livelihoods;
  • Schools and educational institutions;
  • Health and community facilities;
  • Fish processing;
  • Small businesses;
  • Food production;
  • Local economic development; and
  • Climate resilience.

Many low-income African countries continue to face serious challenges related to water availability, water quality and the governance of water services. These difficulties may be particularly severe in rural areas where communities are geographically dispersed and public institutions have limited financial, technical or administrative capacity.

Climate change can intensify these pressures by affecting rainfall patterns, water availability, drought frequency, flooding, groundwater recharge and competition among different water users.

The project is based on the understanding that water possesses characteristics that distinguish it from many other natural resources. It is essential for survival, shared across communities and sectors, affected by geographic and climatic conditions, and often governed by multiple public and community institutions.

Effective water governance must therefore balance:

  • Sustainability;
  • Efficiency;
  • Equity;
  • Affordability;
  • Public health;
  • Environmental protection;
  • Institutional accountability;
  • Community participation; and
  • Competing household and commercial needs.

Geographic Focus of the PhD Research

The project primarily focuses on countries where Iceland maintains bilateral development cooperation:

  1. Uganda;
  2. Malawi; and
  3. Sierra Leone.

Although all three countries form part of the broader research context, the vacancy notice indicates that the doctoral research will place particular emphasis on Uganda.

The doctoral researcher is expected to have working facilities at the University of Iceland in Reykjavík. However, the position also involves conducting necessary data collection in Iceland’s African partner countries in cooperation with the doctoral committee.

Applicants should therefore be prepared for a research design that may require:

  • International fieldwork;
  • Engagement with government authorities;
  • Consultation with rural communities;
  • Interviews with water users and service providers;
  • Collection of policy and institutional data;
  • Collaboration with local organizations;
  • Cross-cultural research;
  • Ethical fieldwork procedures; and
  • Communication with stakeholders across different professional and social backgrounds.

The advertisement does not specify the number, length or financial arrangements for field visits. Candidates should seek clarification from the contact person about travel expectations, insurance, fieldwork funding, security arrangements and institutional support.

Interdisciplinary Academic Environment

The doctoral researcher will work with an interdisciplinary doctoral committee whose expertise includes:

  • Natural-resource management;
  • Development studies;
  • Economics;
  • Social sciences; and
  • Water governance.

This structure reflects the complexity of water governance. The project is not limited to hydrology, engineering or environmental science. It also involves public policy, institutions, development, economics, social relations and the allocation of natural resources.

The successful applicant should be comfortable working across disciplinary boundaries and explaining their research to experts with different academic backgrounds.

Environment and Natural Resources Programme

The position is located within the University of Iceland’s interdisciplinary Environment and Natural Resources programme.

The doctoral researcher may be academically connected to either:

  • The School of Engineering and Natural Sciences; or
  • The School of Social Sciences.

The final academic placement will depend on the research design, supervision arrangements and the successful candidate’s disciplinary background.

The Environment and Natural Resources doctoral programme is an international, interdisciplinary programme connected to the University’s different schools and faculties. It is designed to provide advanced scientific training related to environmental challenges and the sustainable management of natural resources.

The doctoral programme comprises 180 ECTS and is intended to prepare researchers for careers in universities, research institutions, government, international organizations, civil society and other settings requiring advanced research expertise.

Further information is available on the Environment and Natural Resources PhD programme page.

Main Responsibilities of the Doctoral Researcher

The selected candidate will participate in an interdisciplinary research project connected to international development cooperation.

The principal responsibilities include the following.

1. Examine Water-Governance Challenges

The researcher will investigate the major challenges affecting water governance in rural areas of low-income African countries.

This may involve examining:

  • Institutional responsibilities;
  • Water-service planning;
  • Policy implementation;
  • Rural water infrastructure;
  • Financing and maintenance;
  • Community participation;
  • Water affordability;
  • Monitoring systems;
  • Accountability arrangements;
  • Water quality;
  • Unequal access; and
  • Long-term sustainability.

2. Study Water Access for Households and Institutions

The research will consider access to drinking water for:

  • Rural households;
  • Schools;
  • Public institutions;
  • Community facilities; and
  • Other essential users.

This part of the project may require examining how water systems are planned, managed, financed and maintained and whether they provide fair and reliable access to different groups.

3. Examine Water Use in Commercial Activities

The project will also consider water requirements for commercial and productive activities, particularly:

  • Agriculture; and
  • Fish processing.

The researcher may examine how household, institutional and commercial water needs interact and how governance systems allocate water when demand exceeds available supply.

4. Conduct Policy Analysis

The doctoral researcher will assess existing policies, strategies and action plans concerning water governance in selected sub-Saharan African countries.

The analysis may consider:

  • Whether policies clearly assign institutional responsibilities;
  • How national policies are implemented at local level;
  • Whether rural communities participate in decision-making;
  • How water quality and service performance are monitored;
  • Whether policies adequately address sustainability and equity;
  • How development-cooperation projects align with national priorities; and
  • Whether implementation gaps exist between written policies and actual practice.

5. Compare Water-Governance Systems

The researcher will analyse different water-governance arrangements while considering:

  • Environmental sustainability;
  • Institutional effectiveness;
  • Economic efficiency;
  • Social equity;
  • Local ownership;
  • Administrative capacity; and
  • Long-term resilience.

A comparative approach may help identify which governance practices work effectively under particular institutional, geographic and socioeconomic conditions.

6. Apply Interdisciplinary Research Methods

The researcher will use interdisciplinary methods appropriate to the project.

Methods may potentially include:

  • Literature reviews;
  • Policy and document analysis;
  • Stakeholder interviews;
  • Key-informant interviews;
  • Focus-group discussions;
  • Institutional mapping;
  • Comparative case studies;
  • Qualitative data analysis;
  • Field observation;
  • Governance assessments; and
  • Analysis of development-cooperation programmes.

The final methodology will be developed with the doctoral committee and must comply with the University’s academic and ethical standards.

7. Produce Academic Publications

The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to scientific knowledge through:

  • Peer-reviewed journal articles;
  • Conference papers;
  • Academic presentations;
  • Doctoral seminars;
  • Research reports; and
  • A doctoral dissertation.

Candidates should therefore have strong writing skills and the ability to present complex research clearly.

8. Communicate Findings to Policymakers

The project is intended to generate findings that can support governments and other stakeholders in improving water-resource governance.

The researcher will participate in disseminating findings to policymakers and supporting evidence-informed policy development.

This may involve:

  • Policy briefs;
  • Stakeholder workshops;
  • Presentations to government institutions;
  • Discussions with development partners;
  • Accessible research summaries; and
  • Recommendations for strengthening water-governance systems.

Required Academic Qualification

Applicants must possess a master’s degree in a field related to the research topic.

Relevant fields may include:

  • Environmental studies;
  • Natural-resource studies;
  • Social sciences;
  • Development studies;
  • Public policy;
  • Environmental governance;
  • Development economics;
  • Rural development;
  • Political science;
  • Human geography;
  • Sustainability studies; or
  • Another discipline that the applicant can demonstrate is relevant.

The University does not restrict applications only to the disciplines explicitly named in the notice. Candidates with another master’s degree may apply if they can explain its relevance to water governance and the proposed research.

The master’s degree must be completed by the date the position begins.

Required Personal and Professional Competencies

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • The ability to work independently;
  • A disciplined and organized approach to research;
  • Strong communication skills;
  • Strong academic writing skills;
  • Good spoken English;
  • Good written English;
  • The ability to work with an interdisciplinary team;
  • Readiness to engage with policymakers and other stakeholders; and
  • The ability to conduct long-term doctoral research.

Because the project may involve fieldwork in rural communities, candidates should also consider whether they can demonstrate:

  • Cross-cultural communication;
  • Adaptability;
  • Ethical awareness;
  • Sensitivity when working with vulnerable communities;
  • Field-research readiness;
  • Respect for local knowledge; and
  • Ability to work in unfamiliar environments.

These additional qualities are practically relevant, although not all are expressly listed as formal requirements.

Qualifications Considered an Advantage

The following experience or knowledge will strengthen an application but is not presented as mandatory:

Knowledge of Interdisciplinary Research Methods

Applicants with experience combining different disciplinary perspectives may be better prepared for the project.

Qualitative Research Experience

Experience with interviews, focus groups, thematic analysis, case studies, stakeholder consultations or other qualitative methods will be valuable.

Policy-Analysis Experience

The project requires analysis of policies and action plans. Experience evaluating policy design, implementation or institutional performance will therefore be relevant.

Knowledge of Icelandic Development Cooperation

Applicants familiar with Iceland’s bilateral or multilateral development activities in Africa may be able to connect the proposed research more effectively with the project’s institutional context.

Experience in Rural Sub-Saharan Africa

Previous project, professional, voluntary or research experience in rural areas of sub-Saharan Africa will be considered an advantage.

However, the advertisement does not make such experience compulsory.

Icelandic-Language Proficiency

Knowledge of Icelandic is an advantage but is not listed as an essential requirement. The application itself may be submitted in Icelandic or English.

Doctoral Admission Is a Mandatory Condition

Selection for the funded position does not, by itself, complete admission to doctoral studies.

Appointment is conditional upon the successful candidate:

  1. Formally applying to the interdisciplinary doctoral programme in Environment and Natural Resources at the University of Iceland; and
  2. Receiving formal admission approval.

Applicants must therefore satisfy both the employment-selection requirements and the University’s doctoral-admission rules.

The University’s regulations state that the doctoral programme is intended for candidates holding a relevant master’s qualification or an equivalent degree. The board of study assesses whether previous academic preparation is sufficient and may require additional study where necessary.

Required Application Documents

Applications may be submitted in Icelandic or English.

A complete application must contain the following documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

The CV should present the applicant’s:

  • Contact information;
  • Education;
  • Master’s thesis;
  • Research experience;
  • Employment history;
  • Publications, if any;
  • Conference participation;
  • Policy or development-sector experience;
  • Fieldwork experience;
  • Research methods;
  • Language skills;
  • Relevant technical skills; and
  • Awards or professional training.

The vacancy notice does not impose a specific CV page limit.

2. Cover Letter

Applicants must submit a cover letter of no more than two pages.

The cover letter should explain:

  • How the applicant meets the advertised requirements;
  • The relevance of their academic background;
  • Their interest in water governance;
  • Their understanding of the project;
  • Their experience with research methods;
  • Any relevant African field or policy experience;
  • What they can contribute to the project;
  • Why they want to undertake doctoral research at the University of Iceland; and
  • How the position fits their long-term academic or professional objectives.

The two-page limit should be followed strictly.

3. Certified Copies of Diplomas

Applicants must provide certified copies of diplomas from:

  • Undergraduate studies; and
  • Graduate studies.

The notice asks specifically for diplomas rather than a general statement of qualifications. Candidates should check whether academic transcripts, translations or additional certification will be needed during the doctoral-admission stage.

4. Two Referees

Applicants must provide contact information for two referees.

Suitable referees may include:

  • A master’s thesis supervisor;
  • A university professor;
  • A research supervisor;
  • A senior professional familiar with the applicant’s work;
  • A development-sector manager; or
  • Another person capable of assessing the applicant’s research potential.

Candidates should obtain permission before listing a referee and ensure that the provided email address and telephone number are current.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the Icelandic State Recruitment System.

Applicants should:

  1. Open the official application portal;
  2. Change the website language to English by selecting the flag in the upper-right corner;
  3. Create an account if they have not previously registered;
  4. Sign in to the recruitment system;
  5. Complete all required personal and professional information;
  6. Upload the curriculum vitae;
  7. Upload the cover letter of no more than two pages;
  8. Upload certified undergraduate and graduate diplomas;
  9. Enter the contact information of two referees;
  10. Review all uploaded documents;
  11. Confirm that the submission is complete; and
  12. Submit before the deadline.

Applicants should not rely solely on the EURAXESS listing. The University’s State Recruitment System is the relevant application channel.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is 4 September 2026.

The University’s English notice does not state a specific closing time or time zone. International applicants should not wait until the final day because differences in time zones or technical problems could prevent successful submission.

Expected Starting Date

The expected starting date is:

1 November 2026, or another date agreed with the University.

Applicants whose degrees, immigration arrangements or existing employment obligations may affect their availability should address the issue honestly during the recruitment process.

Selection and Notification Process

The University states that all applications will receive a response and that applicants will be informed after a decision has been made.

Applications may remain valid for six months after the closing date. This means the submitted application could continue to be considered during that validity period, although it does not guarantee appointment or placement in another vacancy.

Funding and Financial Information

The project is funded for three years by the Icelandic Ministry for Foreign Affairs through the University of Iceland PhD Grants Fund.

However, the public vacancy notice does not specify:

  • The gross salary;
  • The net monthly salary;
  • Tax deductions;
  • Pension contributions;
  • Tuition or registration-fee arrangements;
  • Fieldwork travel allowances;
  • Relocation funding;
  • Housing support;
  • Visa sponsorship;
  • Family allowances; or
  • Research-expense limits.

Applicants should obtain written clarification regarding these matters before accepting an appointment. The term “funded” should not be interpreted as confirmation that every personal, relocation, tuition or fieldwork expense will automatically be covered.

About the University of Iceland

The University of Iceland is a public research university located in Reykjavík. Established in 1911, it is the country’s largest university and one of Iceland’s largest employers.

The University offers nearly 400 programmes at undergraduate, master’s and doctoral levels. It has approximately 14,000 students, including more than 2,000 international students, and employs more than 1,800 staff members.

Its institutional environment emphasizes:

  • Academic freedom;
  • Research quality;
  • Professionalism;
  • International cooperation;
  • Equality;
  • Diversity;
  • Inclusion; and
  • Social impact.

The University’s doctoral programmes are designed to prepare researchers for advanced roles in universities, research institutes, government, industry and civil society.

Support for International Researchers

The University operates an International Staff Services Welcome Centre for newly recruited international researchers, teachers and doctoral students.

The centre provides practical support to incoming international employees and their families on issues connected with moving to Iceland.

International candidates can find more information through the University of Iceland International Staff Services.

This service should not be treated as confirmation that relocation expenses or immigration sponsorship will be provided. Candidates should distinguish practical relocation guidance from financial support.

Equality and Diversity

The University states that its equality policy is considered during recruitment. It seeks to maintain an international academic environment in which equality, diversity and inclusion are prioritized.

Candidates are assessed against the position’s academic, research and professional requirements. No restriction based on race, ethnicity or gender appears in the vacancy notice.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Applicants should tailor every part of the application to the specific water-governance project.

A strong application should:

  1. Explain how the applicant’s master’s degree relates to water governance;
  2. Describe the applicant’s master’s research or thesis;
  3. Identify relevant research methods;
  4. Demonstrate understanding of rural water-governance challenges;
  5. Explain any experience in sub-Saharan Africa;
  6. Describe policy-analysis experience;
  7. Demonstrate an ability to work across disciplines;
  8. Discuss experience engaging with communities, public institutions or development partners;
  9. Explain the applicant’s interest in Uganda, Malawi and Sierra Leone;
  10. Show how the applicant can translate research into policy-relevant findings;
  11. Demonstrate strong English writing and communication;
  12. Identify realistic contributions to the research project;
  13. Keep the cover letter within two pages;
  14. Provide properly certified academic documents; and
  15. select referees who can assess research ability and professional reliability.

Candidates without previous professional experience in sub-Saharan Africa should not claim experience they do not have. Instead, they should demonstrate transferable research skills, knowledge of development and water-governance literature, cultural sensitivity and readiness for international fieldwork.

Contact for Further Information

Questions about the research project or position may be directed to:

Jón Geir Pétursson
Email: jgp@hi.is

Applicants should use the contact email for substantive questions that are not already answered in the vacancy notice.

Official Links

  • EURAXESS Vacancy 460279
  • University of Iceland Vacancies
  • Official Application Portal
  • Environment and Natural Resources Programme
  • University of Iceland Doctoral Studies

For more global opportunities, click HERE.

Conclusion

The University of Iceland’s funded PhD position in water governance offers an important opportunity to undertake interdisciplinary research with direct relevance to public policy, sustainable development and rural livelihoods.

The project will examine how low-income African countries can strengthen the sustainability, efficiency and equity of rural water-governance systems. Its geographic emphasis on Uganda, Malawi and Sierra Leone, combined with field-based data collection and policy engagement, makes it particularly suitable for candidates interested in connecting academic research with practical development challenges.

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree by the starting date, demonstrate strong English communication and research skills, submit all required documents, and obtain separate admission to the University’s Environment and Natural Resources doctoral programme.

The application deadline is 4 September 2026. Because the recruitment notice does not specify a closing time or time zone, early submission is strongly recommended.

item.content:encoded:
The Michigan Society of Fellows 2026–2029 Postdoctoral Fellowships offer an exceptional opportunity for recent Ph.D. graduates to advance their academic careers through research, teaching, mentorship, and collaboration at the University of Michigan. The prestigious fellowship program brings together promising early-career scholars across the humanities, arts, sciences, and professions, providing them with an intellectually stimulating environment in which to develop their research and teaching careers. The fellowship is designed for scholars who have demonstrated strong academic potential and who are interested in contributing to the intellectual community of a major research university. Successful applicants will receive appointments that combine roles as Assistant Professors in relevant academic departments and Postdoctoral Scholars in the Michigan Society of Fellows. The appointment will last for three years, beginning on August 31, 2026, giving selected fellows substantial time to develop their research agendas, strengthen their teaching experience, collaborate with colleagues, and establish themselves as independent scholars.

About the Michigan Society of Fellows Postdoctoral Fellowship

The Michigan Society of Fellows is inviting applications for its 2026–2029 fellowship cohort, continuing its commitment to supporting outstanding scholars at an early stage of their academic careers. The program provides more than simply a temporary research position. Fellows become part of an academic community where they can engage with researchers and educators from different disciplines while benefiting from the resources and intellectual environment of the University of Michigan. For recent Ph.D. graduates, this type of appointment can provide an important bridge between doctoral study and a long-term academic career. Fellows have the opportunity to deepen their scholarship while also gaining valuable experience in university teaching and academic service.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to scholars who want to develop a strong academic profile that combines:

  • High-quality independent research
  • University-level teaching
  • Interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Academic service
  • Public engagement and outreach
  • Research addressing important contemporary challenges

What Does the Fellowship Offer?

Selected fellows will hold appointments in two connected capacities. They will serve as Assistant Professors in appropriate University of Michigan departments while also being appointed as Postdoctoral Scholars within the Michigan Society of Fellows. This structure provides fellows with the opportunity to participate actively in departmental academic life while remaining connected to the broader Society of Fellows community. The three-year appointment is scheduled to begin on August 31, 2026. During the fellowship period, successful candidates will have an opportunity to further establish themselves as researchers and educators while working within one of the world’s leading research university environments.

Research, Teaching, Service and Outreach

The Michigan Society of Fellows and the University of Michigan emphasize the importance of scholarship that contributes to addressing major challenges facing society. Applicants are therefore encouraged to explain how their academic activities engage with important social, environmental, and technical challenges. This means that applicants should consider more than simply describing their research topic. A strong application can demonstrate how the candidate’s broader academic profile contributes to meaningful questions and challenges in society.

Applicants may wish to demonstrate relevant connections through:

1. Research

Candidates can explain how their research contributes to understanding or addressing significant problems within their discipline or across disciplines. Applicants should clearly communicate the importance of their research and explain its potential intellectual, practical, environmental, technological, or social significance where applicable.

2. Teaching

Teaching is another important component of an academic career. Applicants should demonstrate their ability to contribute effectively to university education and explain how their teaching interests and approaches complement their academic expertise.

3. Service

Academic service can include contributions to departments, universities, professional organizations, scholarly communities, or other relevant groups. Applicants should consider how their past or proposed service activities demonstrate their willingness to contribute to the broader academic community.

4. Outreach and Public Engagement

The program also encourages applicants to consider how their expertise can reach audiences beyond traditional academic settings. Where relevant, candidates can highlight outreach, community engagement, knowledge-sharing, public scholarship, or other activities through which their work contributes to society.

Eligible Academic Fields and Departments

The fellowship is open across a broad range of disciplines in the humanities, arts, sciences, and professions. A comprehensive list of departments eligible for the upcoming fellowship term was scheduled to become available on August 1, 2025. Because eligibility can depend on the departments participating in a particular fellowship cycle, prospective applicants should consult the official Michigan Society of Fellows information and the relevant departmental requirements before preparing and submitting an application.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The fellowship is particularly suited to recent Ph.D. graduates and early-career scholars who are seeking to develop their academic careers within a major research university.

Potential applicants should consider the opportunity if they:

  • Have recently completed, or are completing, a Ph.D. relevant to an eligible field.
  • Have a strong research profile and a clearly defined scholarly agenda.
  • Are interested in developing their university teaching experience.
  • Want to participate in a collaborative and intellectually diverse academic environment.
  • Can demonstrate potential for meaningful contributions to their academic discipline.
  • Have research, teaching, service, or outreach activities that connect with important social, environmental, or technical challenges.
  • Are interested in building a long-term academic career.

Applicants should carefully review the official fellowship requirements to determine whether their degree, discipline, department, and academic status meet the requirements for the 2026–2029 cohort.

Why This Fellowship Is a Valuable Career Opportunity

A three-year appointment can be particularly valuable for scholars transitioning from doctoral study into independent academic careers. Instead of focusing exclusively on completing research, fellows can use the fellowship period to develop several dimensions of their professional profile simultaneously.

Opportunity to Strengthen Research

The fellowship provides an environment in which early-career researchers can continue developing their scholarly work and advancing their research agendas.

Opportunity to Gain Teaching Experience

Because fellows are appointed as Assistant Professors in relevant departments, the program offers an opportunity to gain meaningful university teaching experience alongside research.

Opportunity to Build an Academic Network

Being part of the Michigan Society of Fellows can connect scholars with researchers and academics from different disciplines, potentially creating opportunities for collaboration, mentorship, and interdisciplinary research.

Opportunity for Interdisciplinary Engagement

The Society’s broad coverage of the humanities, arts, sciences, and professions creates an environment where scholars can interact beyond the boundaries of their primary academic fields.

Opportunity to Address Major Global Challenges

The University of Michigan and the Society encourage scholars to demonstrate how their work can contribute to addressing social, environmental, and technical challenges. This emphasis can be particularly valuable for researchers whose work has interdisciplinary or real-world applications.

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Applications

Because the Michigan Society of Fellows is designed for promising early-career scholars, applicants should use their application to present a clear and coherent academic profile.

A strong application should ideally demonstrate the relationship between the applicant’s:

  1. Research agenda — What important questions does the scholar investigate?
  2. Academic contribution — What does the research add to the field?
  3. Teaching interests — What can the applicant contribute to students and the department?
  4. Service activities — How has the applicant contributed to academic or professional communities?
  5. Outreach activities — How does the applicant connect scholarship with wider communities?
  6. Future potential — How will the fellowship help the applicant develop as an independent scholar?
  7. Broader impact — How does the applicant’s work relate to social, environmental, or technical challenges?

Applicants should also make sure their materials are tailored to the relevant department rather than submitting generic academic statements.
